title: Applied ML & Evals — End-to-end Playbook: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quant Profiles, Regression Triage
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook unifies Redwood Inference’s applied-ML and evaluation practices across the eval harness, prompt & benchmark management, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage. It is intended for ML Engineers, SREs, and Product teams who ship models to serving.

Goals
- Provide a single, reproducible path for model quality verification before and after deployment.
- Reduce regression windows by standardizing tests, thresholds, and triage steps.
- Capture artifacts and telemetry needed to make deployment and rollback decisions quickly.

Scope
- Eval harness CI (unit + integration + perf)
- Canonical prompt sets and benchmark definitions
- Model onboarding checklist and required artifacts
- Quality guardrails and alerting thresholds
- Quantization profiles and validation steps
- Regression triage playbook for incidents and quality alerts

Owners and Contacts
- Document owner: Applied ML team (applied-ml@redwood.internal)
- On-call for eval-harness CI: eng-sre (see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks)
- Model onboarding coordination: Model Onboarding Squad (owner: Miguel Ramirez)
- Escalation: Head of Applied ML (Emily Chen)

1) Eval Harness (purpose & standards)

Purpose
The eval harness (service: eval-harness) runs unit, regression, and integration evaluations every model change and on scheduled nightly runs. The harness must be able to run deterministically across CPU/GPU backends and produce MLflow-style artifacts for traceability.

Required outputs
- Deterministic run artifact (run_id, seed, environment spec)
- Metrics: per-prompt accuracy/score, P95 latency, token cost estimate, failure-rate, hallucination score (if applicable)
- Human-review samples (top 50 failures)
- Serialized prompts and model responses (stored in S3: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/<run_id>/)

SLOs for eval CI
- CI run completion: 95% of nightly runs complete within 2 hours
- Per-eval reproducibility: 99% identical top-10 failure set across repeated runs with same seed

Implementation notes
- Harness repo: git@monorepo:redwood/applied-ml/eval-harness (see README.md for setup)
- Runner: Prefers ephemeral GPU nodes with docker image: registry.redwood/inference-eval:stable
- Command example: 
  
  ./run_eval.sh --model candidate-v2 --prompts prompt-set/saas-qa.yaml --seed 1234 --output s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/$(date +%Y%m%d)-candidate-v2

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

Naming & storage
- Prompt sets live in the canonical repo: git@monorepo:redwood/applied-ml/prompt-sets
- File format: YAML (metadata + examples). Name convention: <domain>-<usecase>-v<semver>.yaml (e.g., saas-qa-v1.yaml)

Minimum metadata for each prompt set (table)
- id: unique-id (string)
- owner: team or person
- domain: e.g., "saas-qna"
- use_case: short string
- created_at / last_updated
- labels/tags (list)
- expected_metric: primary metric and pass threshold (e.g., F1 >= 0.78)

Benchmarking rules
1. Every prompt set must include at least 200 labeled examples for statistical significance for common features, or a plan for progressive labeling.
2. Benchmarks must define primary and secondary metrics (e.g., BLEU / ROUGE / F1 / SARI / human-preference percentage).
3. Baselines: each prompt set must record the current production baseline model and the most recent candidate baseline used during eval.

Example prompt-set header (YAML snippet)
  id: saas-qa-v1
  owner: product-qa
  domain: saas-qna
  expected_metric: human_pref_pct >= 0.65

3) Model Onboarding Guide (checklist & artifacts)

Purpose
A minimal checklist and artifact list that must be completed before a model is eligible for serving on Redwood-hosted endpoints or Dedicated/Private deployments.

Onboarding checklist (required)
1. Model card created (model-card.md) including architecture, tokenizer, training data provenance, and license
2. Eval harness run: successful baseline and candidate runs with artifacts uploaded
3. Performance profile: latency and throughput bench (P50, P95, max batch) for target instance types (g4dn, p4, aws-trn1)
4. Quantization profile (if applying int8/4bit) with validation results
5. Safety scan and prompt-sensitivity tests completed (see quality guardrails)
6. Signature and schema for model inputs/outputs (OpenAPI + sample curl)
7. Rollout plan and SLO targets for serving (defined in onboarding doc)

Required artifacts (artifact keys stored in model registry)
- model-card (markdown)
- eval-run-id(s) (list)
- perf-profile-id
- quant-profile-id (optional)
- safety-scan report id
- approved-by (owner + reviewer)

Sample onboarding command (CLI)
  rwdctl model register --name candidate-v2 --model-path s3://models/candidate-v2/ --card-path ./model-card.md --eval run-20270210-candidate-v2

4) Quality Guardrails (automated + human-in-loop)

Guardrail types
- Deterministic checks: tokenization mismatch, invalid logits, OOM detection (failure-rate threshold: <0.5% per 10k requests)
- Behavioral checks: hallucination score, bias indicators, toxicity filters
- Performance checks: P95 latency SLAs, per-model error budget consumption

Automated thresholds (examples)
- Nightly regression alert: if primary metric drops by >= 3 percentage points relative to baseline AND p-value < 0.05
- Production sliding-window alert: rolling 1h window, if failure_rate > 1% OR latency_p95 > 2x target SLO -> page oncall
- Canary gating: candidate canary must not introduce >0.5% increase in error rate and must meet latency SLOs for 24h

Human-in-the-loop
- Monthly model quality reviews: Applied ML + Product reviewer + Ops
- Any automated alert that affects an SLA or primary metric requires a human triage ticket assigned within 1 business hour.

5) Quantization Profiles (definition, validation, and rollout)

Purpose
Quantization profiles capture the parameter choices and validation results for running models at lower precision (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit). Profiles are used by the runtime kernel selector to choose an execution path.

Profile fields (stored as artifact metadata)
- profile_id (string)
- model_version (string)
- quant_type (e.g., int8, 4bit-ptq, 4bit-q4f16)
- per-layer exceptions (comma-separated layer indices)
- expected_accuracy_delta (e.g., -0.6% top-1)
- validation_run_ids (list of run ids)
- perf_gain_estimate (token_cost_reduction_pct)

Validation steps (summary)
1. Run quantization in isolated environment: quantize-tool --model s3://models/foo --mode q4f16 --out s3://tmp/foo-q
2. Run eval harness on canonical prompt sets (same seeds)
3. Compare metrics vs float baseline: require primary metric delta >= -1.0% (configurable per use-case)
4. Run perf benchmarks: latency P50/P95 and throughput at target batch sizes
5. If hardware-only differences expected, run on target instance types and collect kerneltimings

Quantization rollout policy
- Local testing -> canary (10% traffic, 24h) -> ramp 50% -> full. Each step requires monitoring of: error-rate, primary metric, and latency band. Rollback if any of the following occur:
  - primary metric decline > 1.5% absolute vs baseline
  - error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute
  - latency_p95 > 2x target SLO

6) Regression Triage Playbook (incident response for quality regressions)

Triggering conditions
- Automated regression alert (nightly or production) per guardrails section
- User-reported quality regression with reproducible examples

Triage runbook (numbered steps)
1. Create a triage ticket in INCIDENT-Triage (label: regression). Attach eval-run artifacts and failing examples.
2. Immediate checks (5–15 minutes):
   - Check eval-harness run: run_id, seed, env spec. Re-run quick smoke with same seed if feasible.
   - Confirm whether the regression is isolated to a prompt-set or global.
   - Confirm deployment diffs: model_version, quant_profile, runtime image, config flags.
3. If production impact (SLO breach): page oncall; take traffic control action (route to fallback model or reduce traffic) per routing playbook.
4. Owners to run candidate vs baseline A/B comparisons with full prompt-set. Attach diffs: per-example deltas and top-k failure clusters.
5. If root cause is non-model (infrastructure, tokenization bug, runtime flag), apply immediate fix and validate.
6. If model-caused: decide one of: rollback to previous model, patch model and rerun onboarding, or move forward with a canary after fixes.
7. Postmortem: complete within 7 calendar days if production impact > 1 hour. Postmortem must include corrected tests added to eval harness and retrospective action items.

Artifact collection checklist for triage ticket
- eval-run-id(s), failing prompt examples (min 50), model binary location, quantization profile id, runtime image tag, perf profile id, logs (runtime + kernel timings)

7) Dashboards, Alerts, and Evidence retention

Recommended dashboards (in Grafana)
- Model Quality Overview: primary metrics by model_version and prompt_set, baseline comparisons, trending (90d)
- Canary Health: traffic share, error-rate, latency P50/P95, primary metric delta
- Quantization Impact: model_version x quant_profile cross-filterable charts

Alerting (example alerts)
- eval-nightly-regression-critical: fires when primary metric drop >= 3pp AND p < 0.05
- production-quality-slo-breach: rolling 1h window error_rate > 1% or latency_p95 > 2x SLO

Evidence retention policy
- Eval artifacts: 365 days by default in s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/ (extendable per product team)
- Benchmark datasets and prompt-sets: retained indefinitely in git with tags

8) Continuous improvement & governance

Governance cadence
- Quarterly eval-harness review: Applied ML + Eng Platform to review runtime changes that could affect determinism or metrics
- Semi-annual benchmark audit: ensure prompt sets reflect current product usage and data distribution

Contributions and change process
- Pull requests to prompt-sets repo require: owner approval + one reviewer from Applied ML + one Product reviewer for use-case relevance
- Changes to eval-harness thresholds or statistical testing methods require an ADR and approval from Applied ML leadership

Appendix A — Common CLI snippets
- Run canonical eval: ./run_eval.sh --model candidate-v2 --prompts prompt-sets/saas-qa-v1.yaml --seed 42 --output s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/20270210-candidate-v2
- Quick quant validation: quantize-tool --model s3://models/candidate-v2 --mode q4f16 --out s3://tmp/q
- Register model: rwdctl model register --name candidate-v2 --model-path s3://models/candidate-v2/ --card-path ./model-card.md --eval run-20270210-candidate-v2

Appendix B — Quick reference tables

Quant profile example table (CSV-like)
- profile_id, quant_type, expected_accuracy_delta, perf_gain_estimate, validation_run_ids
- qprof-candidate-v2-q4, q4f16, -0.8%, 34%, run-20270210-candidate-v2

Eval artifact retention table
- artifact_type, location, retention_days
- eval-logs, s3://redwood-evals/logs/, 365
- prompt-sets, git@monorepo:redwood/applied-ml/prompt-sets, indefinite
